### Investment Memo: ALNY — 15 November 2026

**Verdict**: BUY (initiate small, scale in) | Conviction: Medium
**Price Target**: $275 (≈ +67% from current $165.04) — midpoint of Value base-case IV ($250–300), consistent with post-cut sell-side cluster ($225–350, median ~$300)
**Time Horizon**: 12–24 months, re-underwritten at the 11-Feb-2027 print

**Investment Thesis**
Alnylam is the category-defining RNAi platform — 65% FY25 revenue growth, first GAAP-profitable year, 24.3% ROIC, ~$1.6–2.3B net cash, a $1B buyback — trading at a 66% discount to its October-2025 peak after two guidance-driven collapses (−28% July, −25% October). The market is pricing ~12–15% revenue CAGR to 2030 and a mid-20s margin versus a 21% consensus and a 25%+ company target; our base case values it at $250–300, and the bear case ($110–140) is roughly where the stock trades. The fraud thesis is dead (negative accruals, clean FY25 cash conversion, no SEC/DOJ action); what remains is a genuine but non-fatal credibility, concentration and pricing-power problem — so we own the platform, not the guidance, in a deliberately small, staged position.

**Key Findings by Domain**
- **Macro & Sector**: Sector ATTRACTIVE (RNAi/ATTR-CM niche, 11–15% TAM CAGRs, high GalNAc/manufacturing barriers); ALNY is growth leader (+65% vs peer median +9.6%) but margin laggard with a narrowing "strong" position. Macro UNFAVOURABLE: 10Y at 5.13% (19-yr high), Fed hiking bias, firm USD, and the 340B rule hitting 15–20% of Amvuttra volume from 1-Jan-2027. Adverse on valuation, benign on operations.
- **Geopolitical & Legal**: MEDIUM. ~95% OECD revenue (negligible China/Russia); live securities class action (class period from Feb-2026, 5–7 firms) but no SEC/DOJ matter; MFN/IRA pricing risk on a >70% US revenue base; LNP litigation overhang resolved (Moderna dismissed with prejudice, Pfizer won) — upside tail gone, distraction gone.
- **Value**: BUY. ROIC inflection to 24.3%, net cash, multi-year NOL tax shield, DCF base $250–300 vs $165 spot; EV/normalized owner earnings ~21x. Bear case ≈ current price gives favorable asymmetry. Note: trailing P/E 70.8x is meaningless (Q3-26's $16.19 EPS was a $1.87B non-cash deferred-tax release; underlying EPS ~$1.5).
- **Growth**: BUY. 3.4x 2027E sales, 18.4x clean 2027E EPS, PEG 0.88, Rule of 40 = 77.7. Wainua's ATTR-CM failure removed the nearest silencer rival; tafamidis generics pushed to 2031; nucresiran shows best-in-class >92% TTR knockdown. Growth decelerating (96%→67%→17% YoY through 2026 quarters) — the gap to the 25% CAGR target must be earned back.
- **Quantitative Signals**: SELL. Worst-in-peer momentum (12-1 ≈ −47%, 1-yr −63.6%) and volatility (58.8%, 2.1x peers); alpha −77% vs SPY; R² 0.0175 — 98% idiosyncratic, event-driven risk. Quality (ROIC, accruals −4.2%, F-Score 7/9) is genuinely above median. Factor model describes the damage; it doesn't forecast the next catalyst.
- **Financial Risk**: MODERATE. Solvency LOW risk (net cash, current ratio 2.76, no maturities before Sept-2027, 4+ years runway, survives a 20% revenue shock); earnings-quality HIGH risk (GM 85.6%→77.3% TTM, SBC = 66% of OCF, DSO creeping 66→79 days). Altman Z of −0.02 is a book-equity artifact — market-value Z is 2.4–5.7; do not quote it as distress.
- **Non-Financial Risk**: HIGH. 87.5% of product revenue from Amvuttra; two >25% guidance-driven drawdowns in one quarter; ~$19M of officer selling through 2026 with zero officer buys (partly 10b5-1/tax mechanics) vs ~$544K of director buying at $152–157; CLO sale 27 days pre-collapse is a bad-look flag. Governance structure sound (separated CEO/Chair).
- **ESG**: AVERAGE / NEUTRAL. Two FDA untitled letters in 8 months on Amvuttra promotion (April-2026 website misbranding) — a live OPDP tail risk on the franchise carrying ~88% of revenue; a Warning Letter is the escalation trigger. Environmental profile genuinely above peer; not a thesis driver.
- **Alternative Data**: BEARISH. Amvuttra search interest −28% from Jul–Aug peak and stabilizing low; no hiring acceleration; UnitedHealth MA first-line restriction (1-Oct-26) hits Q4 first; estimate cuts "mid-flight, not complete." Supports staged entry, not urgency.
- **Short / Contrarian View**: NO EDGE at $165. Was a short at $400–490; the easy 66% is gone. No manipulation evidence (M-Score growth-driven, TATA −0.042, 1.67x FY25 cash conversion). Re-short only above $250–270. Residual bear case requires a third guidance cut or a CRISPR (Intellia nex-z) catalyst — you are paid nothing to wait against $2B+ net cash and positive FCF.

**Bull Case**
- Category leader in a $25B+ (2034) TTR market with the only silencer holding ATTR-CM mortality outcomes data; competitive field narrowed (Wainua failed, tafamidis LOE to 2031).
- Fortress balance sheet + profitability inflection: net cash, four straight FCF-positive quarters, NOL shield, $1B buyback, directors buying the drawdown.
- Valuation asymmetry: $165 ≈ bear-case floor; base case $250–300; consensus 2030 revenue at a 4x EV/S implies ~88% upside before crediting nucresiran, zilebesiran, or Regeneron pipeline optionality.

**Bear Case**
- Deceleration is real and possibly unfinished: Q3-26 growth +16.7% YoY on slow patient starts, two guidance cuts in six months, alt data says Q4 revenue tracks below consensus ($1.525B).
- Structural margin erosion: gross margin −900bp in two years on mix/royalties/payer pressure, with 340B and MFN/IRA still to land.
- Concentration + binary risk: one molecule = 87.5% of revenue; nucresiran Phase 3 and the Feb-2027 print are genuine third-strike events; Intellia's one-time cure threatens terminal value.

**Key Risks**
1. Third TTR guidance cut at 11-Feb-2027 → confirms penetration wall; thesis-breaking.
2. Gross margin <74% → confirms pricing-power loss.
3. SEC/DOJ escalation of the class action, or an FDA Warning Letter on promotion.
4. Rates: 10Y toward 6% mechanically strips another ~8% of pipeline PV and kills takeout optionality.
5. Estimate dispersion is extreme (2028E EPS $5.24–$27.46); every P/E-based anchor is fragile.

**Portfolio Construction Note**
Initiate **1.0% now at ~$165**, build to a **2.0% cap**: +0.5% post-February print if TTR lands in the $4.2–4.5B range with no third cut; +0.5% below $140 absent thesis invalidation; no adds above $220. Vol-target off 58.8% realized vol, not the 0.55 beta artifact — a 2% weight ≈ a 6–7% position in a market-beta name. Correlations are exceptionally low (SPY 0.13, XBI 0.27), making this a genuine diversifier, but do **not** pair with IONS/BridgeBio/Pfizer/Intellia (cap total ATTR/RNAi thesis exposure at 4%). No mechanical stop — sizing is the stop ($110 hard floor only on mandate). Exits: third guidance cut, GM <74%, SEC subpoena, FDA Warning Letter, nucresiran failure, DSO >85 days. Trim one-third at $250, another at $280–300. **Own the platform, not the guidance — small, scaled, and re-underwritten in February.**

*Flag: the specialist team is structurally split — fundamental camp (Value/Growth/Sector) BUY vs risk camp (Quant/Macro/Alt Data/Non-Fin) SELL/CAUTION — resolved by the Short Analyst's "no edge" and Fin Risk's "balance sheet fine, equity price is not." Conviction is Medium, not High, precisely because both sides are right about different timeframes.*

**Price $165.04 (13-Nov-2026) | Mkt cap $22.2B | EV $20.6B | Net cash $1.63B | Next catalyst: Q4/FY26 print 11-Feb-2027**

---

## 1. Agent Conviction Summary Table

| Agent | View | Conviction | Key Finding |
|---|---|---|---|

---

## 2. Consensus Assessment: **SPLIT** (structurally bimodal)

This is not a disagreement about facts — every agent cites the same numbers. It is a disagreement about **what price already discounts them**.

- **Fundamental camp (BUY):** Value, Growth, Sector — 3 agents, medium-high conviction. Argue $165 prices ~12–15% revenue CAGR and a mid-20s margin, versus guidance of 25%+ and consensus of 21%.
- **Risk/technical camp (SELL/AVOID):** Quant, Macro, Alt Data, Non-Fin — 4 agents. Argue momentum is broken, the estimate revision cycle is incomplete, and the 340B/rate shock is dated and unreflected.
- **The bridge:** Short Analyst — "no edge at $165, no fraud, don't short here" — plus Fin Risk ("balance sheet fine, equity price is not") and Geo/Legal ("Medium, not Critical").

**Critical conflict resolution:** the *fraud* concern is **resolved against the bear** — Short Analyst's forensic work (negative accruals, 1.67x cash conversion in FY25, Beneish driven by growth not manipulation) and Geo/Legal's empty EDGAR enforcement search both clear it. The *disclosure-credibility* concern stands (7 firms investigating, two guidance cuts) but is a **multiple** problem, not a solvency or integrity problem. **The earnings-quality flag is real but non-fatal: strip the $1.87B non-cash tax benefit and Q3-26 underlying EPS is ~$1.5, not $16.19 — anyone quoting a trailing P/E of 70.8x or an "8x P/E" is wrong in opposite directions.**

The honest split: **the value is real, the timing is unproven, and the next 90 days contain a dated policy headwind (340B, 1-Jan-27) and a binary credibility event (11-Feb-27).**

---

## 3. Position Sizing Recommendation: **2.0% of portfolio (initiate 1.0%, reserve 1.0%)**

**Rating band applied:** medium conviction + elevated risk → 1–3%. I land at the low-middle.

**Kelly check:** p(success) ≈ 0.55, upside +52% to base case, downside −25% to bear case → raw Kelly ≈ 38%. That is **unusable** for a single binary biotech and must be overridden. The binding constraints are:

- **Volatility budget:** 58.8% annualized vol vs. ~15–18% for a diversified book. A 2.0% position contributes ~1.2% of standalone portfolio vol — a 2.0% weight is roughly equivalent to a 6–7% position in a market-beta name. This is the real size limit.
- **Binary event risk:** R² vs SPY = 0.0175. Three >18% single-day moves in five months. Diversification logic does not protect this position; only sizing does.
- **Concentration discipline:** 87.5% of revenue from one molecule; adding ALNY to a book that already owns IONS/BridgeBio/Pfizer/Intellia doubles ATTR-CM thesis risk.

**Why not 3%+:** the 11-Feb-27 print is a genuine third-strike risk (two guidance cuts already), and the 340B rule lands 1-Jan-27 against 15–20% of AMVUTTRA volume in the same quarter. Paying up for certainty costs little when the bear case ($110–140) is near spot.

**Why not 0.5% or pass:** net cash $1.63B, FCF positive four straight quarters, ROIC 24.3%, base-case IV $250–300, and a $1B buyback authorized. The downside is bounded by a fortress balance sheet — the shareholder risk is multiple compression, not impairment.

---

## 4. Portfolio Fit Analysis

| Dimension | Assessment |
|---|---|
| **Sector** | Healthcare/Biotech. **Caution:** XBI is +37.6% over 12 months — biotech is *not* cheap as a sector. But ALNY at −64% is a contrarian *within* a hot sector, so it reduces the portfolio's momentum/sector-momentum correlation rather than adding to it. Net: acceptable if healthcare is at or below benchmark. |
| **Correlation (verified)** | **Exceptionally low.** ALNY–SPY **0.132**, ALNY–XBI **0.265**, ALNY–VRTX **0.195**, ALNY–IONS **0.310**. This is a genuine diversifier — near-zero beta to the market (R² 0.0175) means it adds idiosyncratic, not systematic, risk. |
| **Factor exposure** | **Adds negative momentum** (12−1 ≈ −47%, worst of peer set) and **high volatility** (58.8%, 2.1x peers). On forward value it is *cheap* (18.4x 2027E vs MRK 20.3x); on trailing it is expensive (70.8x vs 30.8x peer median, +130%). **This is a deliberate anti-momentum, contrarian-value position — size it as such.** |
| **Concentration risk** | Do **not** pair with IONS, BridgeBio, Pfizer or Intellia in the same book — 0.31 correlation understates the shared ATTR-CM/modality thesis risk. Cap total RNAi/ATTR-CM exposure at 4%. |
| **Rate sensitivity** | Effectively a long-duration asset (nucresiran 2030 launch, brezosiran 2027 pivotal). With the 10Y at 5.13% and a hike bias, this position is a leveraged bet on the long end — a 6% 10Y scenario costs ~8% more of fair value. **This is the single largest portfolio-level risk.** |

---

## 5. Entry Strategy: **Scale in — starter now, majority after 11-Feb-2027**

Do **not** buy the full position at $165. The stock is 10.6% off its 10-Nov low ($149.18) and sitting in a momentum vacuum ahead of two dated events.

- **Tranche 1 — 1.0% now, at market (~$165).** Capture the asymmetry the Value and Growth analysts identify; the stock is at the bear-case valuation and 35–45% below base-case IV.
- **Tranche 2 — 0.5% on Q4 confirmation (post 11-Feb-27)** if TTR revenue lands within $4.2–4.5B and 2027 guidance is *not* cut a third time. This is the credibility re-rating trigger.
- **Tranche 3 — 0.5% on price weakness below $140** (bear-case midpoint), assuming no thesis invalidation. This is the Value Researcher's stated add level.
- **Do not add above $220** (Value Researcher's cap) — that is ~1.33x spot and would consume most of the base-case return.

---

## 6. Risk Management Rules

**Stop-loss:** **No mechanical price stop.** At 58.8% vol with 25% gap risk on earnings, a price stop between $120–135 would be triggered by noise and would have exited the 24-Jun-24 +34% gap. Use **sizing as the stop** (max 2.0%). If a hard floor is required by mandate, use **$110** — the bear-case floor — and expect it to be hit only on a structural thesis break.

**Thesis invalidation — exit on any of these:**
1. **Third TTR guidance cut** at the 11-Feb-27 print (below $4.2B) → confirms structural penetration wall, not launch normalization. **Exit.**
2. **Gross margin below 74%** in any quarter → confirms structural loss of pricing power (trajectory: 85.6% → 81.8% → 77.3% TTM → 75.2% Q3-26).
3. **SEC subpoena or 8-K disclosing a formal SEC/DOJ inquiry** → flips legal risk from Medium to Critical. **Exit.**
4. **FDA Warning Letter** on AMVUTTRA promotion (escalation from two untitled letters) → franchise-level commercial risk on 87.5% of revenue.
5. **Nucresiran Phase 3 failure** or a pivotal design rejection → removes the 2030+ franchise.
6. **DSO above 85 days** or AR growth >1.5x revenue growth → channel-stuffing / receivables-quality signal.
7. **Combined exec insider selling without offsetting officer purchases** through a further drawdown → governance signal.

**Trim triggers:**
- **$250** (low end of base-case IV) — trim one-third.
- **$280–300** (base-case midpoint) — trim another third; reassess remaining.
- **>3.0% of portfolio** on appreciation — rebalance to target regardless of price.

**Calendar risk markers:** 1-Jan-2027 (340B rule; Q4 is first full quarter of UHC MA restriction), 11-Feb-2027 (Q4/FY26 + 2027 guidance), 2027 (nucresiran Phase 3 topline; brezosiran pivotal design).

---

## 7. Final Portfolio Action: **INITIATE (partial — 1.0% now, build to 2.0%)**

**Rationale.** The specialist split resolves in favor of ownership but against urgency. The fraud thesis is dead (negative accruals, clean FY25 cash conversion, no EDGAR enforcement action), the balance sheet is fortress-grade ($1.63B net cash, no maturities to Sept-2027, 4+ years of runway), and the base-case discount to intrinsic value is 35–45%. Against that: momentum is broken and possibly not finished (Alt Data: "estimate cuts mid-flight, not complete"), the macro tape is actively hostile to long-duration assets (10Y 5.13%), and two dated events — the 340B rule and the February print — sit inside the next 90 days.

**This is a 2.0% core position with a 1.0% starter, not a 5% conviction buy.** The low correlation to SPY (0.13) and XBI (0.27) makes it a legitimate diversifier; the 58.8% volatility and binary event risk make anything larger imprudent. The asymmetry is real — bounded downside on a cash-rich balance sheet, ~50–80% upside to base case — but it must be *earned back* quarter by quarter, starting 11 February 2027.

**One-line verdict:** *Own the platform, not the guidance — small, scaled, and re-underwritten at the February print.*

## SECTOR BRIEF — ALNY (Alnylam Pharmaceuticals)
**Sub-sector: RNAi therapeutics / rare-disease & cardio-metabolic biotech** (GICS "Healthcare" → "Biotechnology"; the broad Healthcare tag is misleading — peers must be drawn from biotech, not payers/distributors)

---

### 1. Sector Overview
Alnylam competes in the RNAi/siRNA modality niche nested inside the ~$2.4T (top-25 company sample) Healthcare complex. It is one of the few genuine growth pockets in an otherwise maturing large-cap biotech industry: FY2025 revenue growth was 65% for ALNY and 34% for Ionis, versus 9.6% (Vertex), 1.4% (Biogen) and 1.0% (Regeneron) — i.e., the legacy biotech cohort is in a patent-cliff/mature phase while the RNAi modality is still early-to-mid growth (global RNAi market ~$3.6B in 2026 → ~$9.1B by 2035, ~11% CAGR). The commercial centre of gravity is ATTR amyloidosis (TTR silencers + stabilisers), forecast to grow from a ~$6–7B amyloidosis market today to ~$35B by 2035 (~14.6% CAGR), with ATTR-CM alone projected at up to ~$64B by 2033 on diagnosis-rate expansion. The sector has shifted from monopoly to oligopoly in 24 months (tafamidis 2019 → acoramidis Nov-2024 → vutrisiran Mar-2025 → eplontersen/next-gen entrants + one-shot CRISPR), so rivalry — not demand — is now the binding constraint. Capital intensity is high (oligo manufacturing, global commercial infrastructure) but R&D/delivery-chemistry IP remains a real barrier to entry.

### 2. Key Tailwinds
- **ATTR-CM diagnosis pool expansion + outcomes evidence.** Only ~5,000–7,000 new US ATTR-CM diagnoses per year against a far larger prevalent pool; new 5-year HELIOS-B open-label-extension data (AHA, Nov-2026) show sustained mortality/morbidity benefit for vutrisiran — supportive of guideline positioning and duration of therapy.
- **Modality diversification past TTR.** Zilebesiran (hypertension, annual/semi-annual dosing), Regeneron-partnered CIDEBsiRNA (first-in-human MASLD data showed liver-fat normalisation after a single dose, Nov-2026), plus CNS/ocular — each a multi-billion TAM where ALNY retains economics or royalties.
- **Profitability inflection + capital return.** FY2025 was ALNY's first GAAP-profitable year (op. income $502M, 13.5% margin); a **$1B buyback** authorised Nov-2026 signals durable FCF — a rare signal in small/mid biotech and a support for per-share value.

### 3. Key Headwinds
- **ATTR-CM price/ share war.** Tafamidis ~$268k/yr, acoramidis ~$244k, patisiran ~$450k, vutrisiran ~$477k list. Acoramidis real-world data (HFSA, Sept-2026) positioned it favourably vs tafamidis; Intellia's one-time gene editing (nex-z) is a structural substitute threat to chronic silencers. HHI in ATTR is falling fast — top-3 share still ~85–90% but pricing power is eroding.
- **Demand deceleration / credibility damage at ALNY specifically.** Q3-2026 revenue growth slowed to **+16.7% YoY** ($1,458M vs $1,249M) from +66.8% in Q2 and +96.4% in Q1, on slower Amvuttra patient starts. Shares fell −28% (30-Jul-26) and −25% (29-Oct-26); securities-fraud investigations opened (Pomerantz, Glancy Prongay) and commercial leadership changed — an overhang on the whole RNAi complex's valuation multiple.
- **Gross-margin compression + IRA/payer pressure.** Q3-2026 gross margin **75.2%** vs 84.2% a year earlier (COGS 24.8% of revenue vs 19.2% in FY2025) on partner royalties and manufacturing scale-up; Medicare Part D redesign, inflation rebates and negotiated pricing constrain realised net price on $450k+ therapies.

Position vs peers: **growth leader, margin laggard, second-tier multiple (5.9x sales already de-rated from ~15x).**

Structurally growing demand (diagnosis penetration), 11–15% TAM CAGRs, high barriers (GalNAc delivery IP, oligo manufacturing), and a visible profitability inflection justify an Attractive rating for the modality. The rating is capped by oligopolistic rivalry in ATTR-CM, one-shot gene-editing substitution risk, and IRA-driven net-price erosion. The alpha in this sector over the next 24 months will come from **share capture and durability of ATTR-CM patient starts**, not from multiple expansion — which is precisely the variable ALNY is currently being penalised for.
